title: CSV Log Integrity Discipline
description: CSV log integrity discipline for the PRISMA and non-PRISMA logs of the correctness-wedge review, plus their linked corpora (abstract markdowns and Track 2 decision markdowns). Codifies the stable_id column, immutable manual IDs, atomic writes with lockfile discipline, logs-index synchronisation, and the corpus-linkage contracts enforced by csv_lint.py. Supersedes the ad-hoc conventions previously carried only inside CLAUDE.md and the individual skill SKILL.md files.

body_md:
# CSV Log Integrity Discipline

This file governs the six logs indexed by `logs-index.csv` and the two markdown corpora that link back to them. It codifies the rules that prevent the failure class documented under "Fiasco reference" below.

## Scope

Six primary CSVs (four PRISMA, two non-PRISMA) plus one auxiliary CSV:

| Log | Path | Row grain |
|---|---|---|
| `01a_identification_all.csv` | `logs/prisma-logs/` | one row per (reference, Consensus query) hit |
| `01b_identification_track2_anchors.csv` | `logs/prisma-logs/` | one row per Track 2 purposive-selection anchor |
| `01c_identification_dedup.csv` | `logs/prisma-logs/` | one row per Track 1 unique reference (post-dedup) |
| `2b_screening_excluded.csv` | `logs/prisma-logs/` | one row per screening exclusion |
| `ch3_methods_anchors.csv` | `logs/non-prisma-logs/` | one row per Chapter 3 methodology anchor |
| `signpost_citations.csv` | `logs/non-prisma-logs/` | one row per signpost / framing citation |
| `manual_abstracts.csv` | `logs/prisma-logs/` | one row per manually-supplied abstract, keyed by canonical DOI |
| `prisma-tally.csv` | `logs/` | one row per PRISMA funnel node; live-state, `count` column mutates in place |

Two linked corpora that must stay in sync with the above:

| Corpus | Path | Linked to |
|---|---|---|
| Abstract markdowns | `abstracts/*.md` | `01c` via filename digest and `abstract_location` |
| Track 2 decision markdowns | `prisma-track2-inclusion-decisions/*.md` | `01b` via `inclusion_decision_path` |

## Fiasco reference (2026-09-02)

Two overlapping `fetch_abstracts.py` runs produced ~450 markdown files where only 231 were canonical, because the previous filename scheme was keyed on the positional `unique_ref_id` column. `unique_ref_id` is assigned by row position after a stable sort in `extract_consensus_refs.py`, so adding Q17-Q22 to the Consensus batch shifted almost every `U####` and orphaned the entire previous abstract corpus. Recovery required a full workspace reload, manual `Stop-Process`, and a `.tmp_plans/migrate_abstract_filenames.py` sweep.

The rules below prevent that failure class from recurring — for any log, whether or not it has an equivalent linked corpus.

## Rule 1 - `stable_id` is the join key on every log

Every row in every log carries a `stable_id` column immediately after the log's human-readable ID column (`ref_id`, `unique_ref_id`, `anchor_id`, `signpost_id`, ...). The human-readable ID is retained for display and scanning but MUST NOT be relied upon by any script for joins or filename derivation.

The `stable_id` is a lowercase 8-hex-char MD5 prefix of the row's identity key. The identity key is derived as:

```
if doi_url is non-empty:
    identity_key = "doi:" + canonical_doi(doi_url)
elif title is non-empty:
    identity_key = "title:" + normalise_title(title) + "|year:" + year
elif full_citation is non-empty (01b, ch3, signposts):
    identity_key = "citation:" + normalise_title(full_citation)[:60] + "|year:" + year
else:
    identity_key = "unknown:" + row_display_id + "|year:" + year
```

with:

- `canonical_doi(url)` strips `https://`, `dx.`, `doi.org/`, lowercases, and trims trailing punctuation.
- `normalise_title(s)` NFKD-normalises, drops non-ASCII, lowercases, and keeps only `[a-z0-9]`.

For `01a`, whose row grain is (reference, query), `stable_id` is derived from paper identity ONLY (do not include `query_id` in the digest). This means `stable_id` in `01a` can repeat across rows that share the same paper but differ by `query_id`; the row uniquer in `01a` is the composite `(stable_id, query_id)`.

For every other log, `stable_id` is unique per row and is enforced by `csv_lint.py`.

`stable_id` is content-derived, not positional. Adding rows, deleting rows, or re-running the pipeline never shifts it. It survives Consensus batch expansion, DOI-only edits that fix truncations, and re-sorts.

## Rule 2 - manual IDs are immutable

Rows in `01b`, `ch3_methods_anchors`, and `signpost_citations` carry human-assigned identifiers (`T2-A01`, `T2-B03`, `CH3-01`, `SG-05`, ...). These IDs are **immutable once written**. They MUST NOT be recycled, renumbered, or reassigned. In particular:

- Deleting a row does not free its ID. The gap remains as a permanent tombstone.
- If a row must be logically removed, add a `status=retired` column value (or move the row to a `retired/` subfolder within the same log family, preserving its identifier) and NEVER reassign the vacated slot to a new anchor.
- New rows get the next unused number for their block. `T2-A09` was the highest in Block A on 2026-09-02; the next Block A anchor is `T2-A10`, never `T2-A05` even if `T2-A05` was retired.

This preserves the referential integrity of every decision markdown, external citation, and downstream reference that pins to the ID.

## Rule 3 - atomic writes and lockfile discipline

Every script that mutates any of the six logs MUST:

1. Write the new content to `<log>.tmp` in the same directory.
2. Call `os.replace(tmp, target)` to atomically swap.
3. Acquire a lockfile at `<log>.pid` (or a shared lockfile for scripts that mutate multiple logs) before starting. The lockfile contains the writing process's PID and start timestamp.
4. Refuse to start if the lockfile is present and the PID is still alive on the local machine. Print an error identifying the running PID.
5. Release the lockfile (delete it) on normal exit AND install a `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` handler to release it on interrupt.

Google Drive syncs the `.tmp` and `.pid` files as normal blobs; they do not corrupt the CSV even under sync races.

`fetch_abstracts.py` and `extract_consensus_refs.py` both fall under this rule.

## Rule 4 - `logs-index.csv` is the manifest of record

`logs-index.csv` at `logs/` describes every CSV in `logs/prisma-logs/` and `logs/non-prisma-logs/`. It carries these columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `log_name` | Filename on disk. MUST exist. |
| `path` | Subdirectory (`prisma-logs/` or `non-prisma-logs/`). |
| `category` | `prisma` or `non-prisma` or `reference-data`. |
| `purpose` | One-sentence description. |
| `unique_id_column` | Human-readable display ID column name (e.g. `unique_ref_id`, `anchor_id`). Comma-separated if compound. |
| `id_derivation` | `positional_display_only + stable_id_content` for content-derived IDs, `manual_immutable + stable_id_content` for T2/CH3/SG anchors, `external` for the SJR reference dataset. |
| `robustness_class` | `content_derived_stable`, `manual_immutable`, or `external_stable`. |
| `created_date` | dd-mm-yyyy. |

Any file rename touching a log MUST update `logs-index.csv` in the SAME commit. `csv_lint.py` fails the commit otherwise. If a log is retired, its row stays in the index with a `status=retired` note appended to `purpose`.

## Rule 5 - abstracts corpus contract

Files under `abstracts/*.md` are linked to `01c_identification_dedup.csv`.

- Filename shape: `{year}_{surname}_{stable_id}.md` where `stable_id` is the 8-hex-char MD5 prefix of `01c.dedup_key`.
- The markdown Provenance block MUST include a `- **dedup_key**: ...` line matching the CSV row.
- The `- **doi**: ...`, `- **year**: ...`, and `- **authors**: ...` provenance lines MUST match the CSV row.
- The `01c.abstract_location` column MUST resolve to a real file under `abstracts/`, OR carry one of these sentinels:
  - `unavailable` (no source returned an abstract)
  - `track2_anchor:<T2-XXX>` (paper is a Track 2 anchor; abstract not needed)
  - `excluded:<reason>` (paper matched the exclude list; abstract not fetched)
- Files whose corresponding CSV row has become a sentinel MUST be moved to `abstracts/_orphans/`, not deleted, so the audit trail is preserved.

## Rule 6 - Track 2 decisions corpus contract

Files under `prisma-track2-inclusion-decisions/*.md` are linked to `01b_identification_track2_anchors.csv`.

- Filename shape: `{anchor_id}_{surname}_{year}.md` (e.g. `T2-A01_acemoglu_restrepo_2018.md`).
- The `01b.inclusion_decision_path` column MUST resolve to a real file, expressed relative to the `consensus-queries/` folder.
- The file's H1 heading MUST start with the anchor_id (e.g. `# T2-A01 - Acemoglu & Restrepo (2018), ...`).
- The file's `**DOI:**` line MUST canonicalise to the CSV row's `doi_url`.
- Rejected candidates live under `prisma-track2-inclusion-decisions/rejected/`. They are NOT required to appear in `01b`, but their filenames still start with the retired anchor_id and their content documents why the candidate was dropped.
- If a Track 2 anchor is retired, the decision markdown is moved to `rejected/` (preserving filename) rather than deleted.

## Rule 7 - enforcement

`.github/skills/consensus-search-log/scripts/csv_lint.py` is the mechanical enforcement layer. It:

- Verifies every log has a `stable_id` column populated on every row.
- Verifies `stable_id` uniqueness where required (all logs except `01a`).
- Verifies `2b.stable_id` (or DOI) matches a row in `01c`.
- Runs the abstracts corpus contract (Rule 5) end to end.
- Runs the Track 2 decisions corpus contract (Rule 6) end to end.
- Verifies `logs-index.csv` filename entries resolve to real files.
- Verifies no manual IDs have been reassigned (compares against a committed baseline).
- Runs the manual abstracts overlay contract (Rule 8) end to end.
- Runs the PRISMA tally contract (Rule 9) end to end.

`csv_lint.py` MUST be run and MUST exit zero before any commit that touches the paths in this file's `applyTo` glob. In practice this is enforced by the developer running it locally; there is no CI on this repo.

## Rule 8 - manual abstracts overlay

`manual_abstracts.csv` at `logs/prisma-logs/` supplies abstracts (and any other future overlay values) for rows where the Consensus CSV export left the Abstract column empty. It is joined into 01c by `extract_consensus_refs.py` at run time; the underlying Consensus CSVs are never mutated.

Schema:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stable_id` | 8-hex MD5 prefix of `doi:<canonical_doi>`. Must equal `01c.stable_id` for the same DOI. |
| `doi_url` | Full `https://doi.org/...` URL. The join key. |
| `abstract` | Cleaned abstract text. Inline `[text](url)` markdown links MUST be stripped on ingest to match the plain-text convention of the abstracts corpus. |
| `source_url` | Optional. Where the text was retrieved from (may match `doi_url` or point at a specific ScienceDirect / publisher URL). |
| `added_date` | dd-mm-yyyy of when the row was written. |

Precedence order when both sources supply an abstract for the same DOI: Consensus CSV wins, manual overlay ignored. The overlay is a rescue layer for the empty case, not an override.

`fetch_abstracts.py` writes markdowns for these rows with `abstract_src = manual` in the provenance block, distinguishing them from the four API sources (`crossref`, `semantic-scholar`, `openalex`, `arxiv`) and from `consensus_csv`.

`csv_lint.py` verifies for every row: `doi_url` non-empty, canonical DOI resolves to a 01c row, declared `stable_id` matches `01c`'s computation, `abstract` non-empty.

## Rule 9 - PRISMA running tally

`prisma-tally.csv` at `logs/` is the single live-state view of the PRISMA funnel. One row per node; the `count` column mutates in place as the review progresses; no append-only history is kept in this file (git history plus the individual log CSVs are the audit trail).

Schema:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stable_id` | 8-hex MD5 prefix of `node_id`. Uniquely identifies the node across renames of `label`. |
| `node_order` | Integer, ascending in PRISMA display order. |
| `prisma_stage` | One of `identification`, `screening`, `eligibility`, `included`. |
| `track` | One of `track1`, `track2`, `combined`. |
| `node_id` | Immutable machine identifier (snake_case). MUST NOT be renamed once written. |
| `label` | Human-readable text for reports. May be revised. |
| `count` | Integer or empty. Empty means "not yet observed"; do not fill with zero unless the count really is zero. |
| `source_log` | The log CSV or derivation formula the count comes from (e.g. `01c_identification_dedup.csv`, `computed: 01a - 01c`). |
| `last_updated` | ISO date (yyyy-mm-dd) of the most recent `count` write. |
| `notes` | Free text. |

`csv_lint.py` verifies for every row: `node_id` present and unique, declared `stable_id` equals `md5(node_id)[:8]`, `count` is an integer if non-empty. Renaming a `node_id` breaks referential intent and is a lint failure by construction (the recomputed stable_id will no longer match the on-disk value).

New nodes are appended; existing rows are updated in place. When a stage completes, backfill the terminal counts and update `last_updated`.

## Rule 10 - pipeline_status column (soft-delete for PRISMA scope)

Any of the six primary log CSVs MAY carry an optional `pipeline_status` column. When present, values MUST be drawn from the following enumeration:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `active` | Row participates in every downstream count, dedup, join, tally, and site render. Default when the column is absent. |
| `ignored_optional_q15` | Row belongs to an optional Consensus query (Q15) that the reviewer decided post-retrieval NOT to operationalise. Row is retained on disk for audit; every downstream tool MUST filter it out before counting. |

Add-only extension. Future ignore reasons get their own enumerated values (`ignored_optional_qNN`, `ignored_scope_pivot_...`, etc.) so downstream tools can distinguish reasons without regex.

Filtering contract: any script that consumes a log with `pipeline_status` MUST filter to `pipeline_status == 'active'` before counting, joining, or writing derived artefacts. This is the "soft-delete for PRISMA scope" pattern: rows never disappear, they just stop counting.

Symmetry across logs: when a row is marked `ignored_...` in one log, the same paper (by `stable_id`) is either absent from downstream logs or carries the same status. For Q15, this means 01a, 01c, and 2b all carry the 20 Q15-primary rows marked `ignored_optional_q15`.

`csv_lint.py` verifies for every log that has the column: every row has a non-empty `pipeline_status` value, and every value is in the allowed enumeration. Missing / out-of-set values are lint failures.

## History

- 2026-09-02 - file created after the fetch_abstracts orphan-file fiasco. Codifies the discipline needed to keep the six logs and their two linked corpora in provable sync. Supersedes any earlier ad-hoc CSV conventions carried inside `CLAUDE.md` or the individual skill SKILL.md files, per the freeze policy in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` Section 0.5.
- 2026-09-02 - Rule 8 added for the `manual_abstracts.csv` overlay. Seeded with 6 rows for Elsevier DOIs that returned 404 across all API sources.
- 2026-09-03 - Rule 9 added for `prisma-tally.csv`. Live-state PRISMA funnel view seeded with 14 nodes (identification, screening, eligibility, included) from today's 01a/01b/01c/2b counts. `csv_lint.py` extended with tally integrity check.
- 2026-09-03 - Rule 10 added for the `pipeline_status` column. Introduced when Q15 was reclassified as a not-operationalised optional query rather than a scope exclusion. 20 rows across 01a, 01c, and 2b now carry `pipeline_status = 'ignored_optional_q15'`; active pool for AI screening is 307 (312 unique - 5 Track-2 overlaps).
